Three-person corner saunas here start at $3,899. A corner cabin exists for one reason: it uses two walls you already have, so it fits a room where a rectangular cabin of the same interior volume will not.

The measurement that decides it

A corner unit is measured along its two wall-facing sides, not across the front, so comparing a corner cabin's footprint to a rectangular one by width alone will mislead you. Measure the two walls you intend to use, check the door swing, and confirm the diagonal clearance you need to get the panels into the room before the cabin arrives. That last one is where corner installations go wrong: a narrow hallway or a tight stair turn will stop a panel that the finished footprint would have fitted.

Heat and power

These are infrared cabins running at 120 to 140°F, so sessions run longer and cooler than a traditional room. Most publish a standard 120V outlet as their requirement, which is why a corner cabin is often the practical choice for a spare bedroom or a finished basement. Both Canadian hemlock and western red cedar appear here.

Standard delivery is free to the lower 48 and is curbside drop-off. That matters more than usual for a corner unit: the panels have to reach the corner you have measured, so check the doorways, the stair turn and the hallway width before delivery day. Inside delivery is $600, and $1,800 covers inside delivery with unboxing and full assembly.

If a corner is not a constraint for you, the two-person infrared cabins start lower, and indoor infrared saunas covers the wider range.
